explicit_validation.explanation: Paper conducts systematic validation where automated LLM evaluation (HAMLET pipeline using GPT-4o/GPT-4o-Mini) is quantitatively compared against expert human judgments on the same instances for key-fact alignment (recall) and fact-checking (faithfulness)

prompts.notes: Exact prompts shown in appendix tables (Tables 12 and 13) for analytical and narrative key-fact tree generation; validation uses adapted FINESURE pipeline prompts detailed in Appendix E

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Experts resolved disagreements through discussion to consensus label

guidelines.notes: Evaluation criteria clearly defined in Section 4: key-fact alignment (binary: whether each key-fact appears in summary) and fact-checking (binary: whether each summary sentence is supported by source)

sample_size.notes: Used 600 instances (sampled from total 4,884+632 summaries) for validation - 300 for key-fact alignment (recall) and 300 for fact-checking (faithfulness)

quantitative_scores.notes: Binary accuracy for key-fact alignment task
Binary accuracy for key-fact alignment task

validation_results.summary_finding: HAMLET's automated pipeline achieves over 90% agreement with expert human judgments (98.1% recall accuracy, 91.6% faithfulness accuracy with GPT-4o), outperforming crowd-sourced workers and FINESURE baseline while reducing cost by 25×

criteria_mapping.notes: Humans additionally validated intermediate components (key-fact trees and queries) while LLM and human both evaluated final summaries on recall and faithfulness
